name: TAN
description: TAN returns the tangent of a given angle. The angle must be expressed in radians.
tldr: Returns the tangent of an angle given in radians.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The angle, in radians, for which you want the tangent.

basicExample.explanation: RADIANS(45) is π/4; the tangent of π/4 is 1.

advancedExamples.title: Tangent of π/4
advancedExamples.explanation: The tangent of π/4 radians (45°) is 1.

howItWorks: TAN computes the tangent of an angle measured in radians, equivalently SIN(number)/COS(number). The function is periodic with period π and is undefined (returns a very large magnitude) at π/2 + kπ, where cosine is zero.

howToSteps.name: Convert if needed
howToSteps.text: If your angle is in degrees, wrap it with RADIANS().

howToSteps.name: Enter the formula
howToSteps.text: Type =TAN(number) with the angle in radians.

limitations: The angle must be in radians; degrees must be converted with RADIANS or PI()/180.
Near π/2 + kπ the result grows extremely large (approaching the undefined tangent).
Results are approximate due to floating-point math.

commonErrors.cause: Angle is close to π/2 (90°), where tangent is undefined.
commonErrors.fix: Check the angle; the value is mathematically approaching infinity.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: TAN works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: My TAN gives wrong values — why?
faq.answer: Most likely you passed degrees. Convert with RADIANS() first, e.g. =TAN(RADIANS(45)).

faq.question: What is the period of TAN?
faq.answer: π radians (unlike SIN/COS, which have period 2π).

faq.question: Why is TAN(90°) enormous instead of an error?
faq.answer: At exactly π/2 radians cosine is 0, so TAN = SIN/COS diverges; floating-point gives a very large number rather than an error.
